auditFocus: a blocking call (sync DB driver, `requests`, `time.sleep`, sync file I/O) inside an `async def` path operation or dependency instead of a `def` one FastAPI can offload to its threadpool
a request body or query model that skips Pydantic validation by typing a parameter as `dict`/`Any` instead of a `BaseModel`
a path operation with no `response_model`/return type where one would prevent leaking internal fields (e.g. `hashed_password`) in the response
a dependency-injected auth check (`Depends(get_current_user)`) missing from a path operation that should require it
`CORSMiddleware` configured with `allow_origins=["*"]` alongside `allow_credentials=True`, which browsers reject and which is unsafe if they didn't
secrets/config read from hard-coded values instead of `pydantic-settings`/environment, or a `SECRET_KEY` committed in source
buildCommands: python -c "import <app_module>" # or: uvicorn <app_module>:app --port 0 as an app-startup smoke check
fixGuardrails: never add `# type: ignore` or `# noqa` to silence a checker without fixing or explaining the underlying issue
never move a blocking call into an `async def` path operation to "simplify" it -- keep it `def` so FastAPI's threadpool handles it, or make the call itself async
never widen a Pydantic model's field type to `Any`/`dict` just to make validation errors stop
fix the smallest root cause; do not refactor unrelated code while resolving a build/lint/type failure
